headline: US Fed held its rate at 3.75 to 4.00%
detail: Two members voted for a hike.

headline: Democrats won control of the US House and were set to take the Senate in the midterm elections
detail: Time is the first report found (Variety, about 03:23 UTC, 8:53 am IST); by 4 Nov they had also taken the Senate, gaining five seats.

headline: US stocks sold off sharply from the open, led by AI and chip stocks: Nasdaq about -5% during the day
detail: By 1 pm New York time (18:00 UTC): Nasdaq -5.3%, S&P 500 -4.0%, Dow -3.1%, the chip index -11%; Nvidia -7%, AMD -13%, Micron -13%, Tesla and SpaceX -9%; VIX up 55% to about 26; Bitcoin below $76,000; Brent back near $97. Reports tie it to worries that the new Democratic Congress could limit data-centre building and raise its power and water costs, with no specific proposal named. These are intraday figures, not the close; the close goes in a later row.

headline: US payrolls rose 165,000 in October and unemployment fell to 4.1%
detail: Expected: +59,000 and 4.2%. Average hourly earnings +0.4% m/m, 3.1% y/y (expected 0.3% and 2.9%). August revised up to 186,000 (+53,000), September to 60,000 (+31,000).

headline: US stocks sold off sharply on 5 Nov, led by AI and chip stocks: Nasdaq closed -5.52%
detail: Close figures (replacing the intraday ones in the earlier row): Nasdaq -5.52%, the Dow down about 1,833 points; S&P 500 and Dow had their worst day since April 2025; about $2.5 trillion of market value lost. Reports tie it to fears that Democrats' midterm gains (including a Texas governor-elect who campaigned on a data-centre moratorium) could slow the AI buildout. Time is the US open; the selling built through the day.

headline: Oil fell on an unconfirmed report that Iran eased its Strait of Hormuz demands, with a proposed Hormuz deal going to President Trump, who signalled restraint on Iran despite fresh shipping attacks
detail: Time approximate: the reports are dated 9 Nov and the first report's exact time was not found, so the start of the day (UTC) is used. Reports put Brent near $94, extending its biggest weekly drop since 2020. The report on Iran's demands was unconfirmed.

headline: US consumer prices rose 0.4% in October; core rose 0.3%
detail: Expected (Dow Jones survey): 0.3% headline, 0.2% core. September: 0.6% and 0.3%. No 12-month rates were published for October because October 2025 prices were not collected during the shutdown; they return with the November report on 10 Dec. Last official y/y (September): 3.7% headline, 2.6% core.

headline: Trump said the Iran war was "effectively over" militarily and new strikes looked unlikely, while keeping the naval blockade in place; Brent fell below $90 on 10 Nov for the first time since August
detail: Time approximate: the remark came after oil settled at 2:30 pm New York time on 9 Nov (19:30 UTC); the exact time was not found. Reports put Brent's 10 Nov low at $89.16 and its settle at $91.49 (-1.17%).
